{{Top|leg}}
[[File:WA7waitress-NEGTD.png|thumb|right|250px|The design of the WA-7 waitress droid was heavily influenced by Mondeo Modernism]]
'''Mondeo Modernism''' was a design craze that swept through the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] over a [[Standard century/Legends|century]] before the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]].<ref name="CSWE-Mondeo Mondernist">{{CSWECite|II|327|Mondeo Modernist}}</ref> The fad spread to art, [[Architect/Legends|architecture]], and [[Clothing/Legends|clothing]] design. It emphasized the use of streamlined contours, elliptical forms, and whimsical embellishments. The craze burned brightly for several [[Standard decade/Legends|decades]] but eventually fizzled.<ref name="TNEGtD">''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref>

The [[WA-7 waitress droid/Legends|WA-7 waitress droid]], produced by [[GoCorp/Legends|GoCorp]] and its subsidiary [[Utilitech/Legends|Utilitech]], was introduced at a [[Time/Legends|time]] when the Core Worlds were gripped in the fever of the Mondeo Modernist design movement.<ref name="TNEGtD" /> Its streamlined design suggested the shape of a [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] [[Gender/Legends|female]].<ref name="SWC:TP">''[[Star Wars Chronicles: The Prequels]]''</ref> It also featured [[Color/Legends|dark-red]] decorative elements that gave it an even more fanciful silhouette,<ref name="CSWE-WA-7 series">{{CSWECite|III|317|WA-7 series}}</ref> such as a skirt and a bonnet that projected curved fins behind the head.<ref name="FF">{{FactFile|64|WAI 1-2|WA-7 Waitress Droid}}</ref> The [[Droid/Legends|droid]] moved on a unipod [[wheel]], a concession to the flightiness of Mondeo Modernism that proved quite practical.<ref name="TNEGtD" />

[[Standard year/Legends|Years]] later, many WA-7 [[Service droid/Legends|service unit]]s were still in service and became popcultural artifacts of the Mondeo Modernist era.<ref name="TNEGtD" /> By [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], the WA-7 was considered a throwback to this earlier era of style and design. This made [[FLO/Legends|FLO]], the droid [[Waiter/Legends|waitress]] working at [[Dex's Diner|Dexter's Diner]], seem quite at home in [[Dexter Jettster/Legends|Dexter Jettster's]] [[Med'soto style|retro-style]] [[Restaurant/Legends|diner]].<ref name="FF" />

Shortly before the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the droid manufacturer [[AccuTronics/Legends|AccuTronics]] briefly attempted to play off the retro-popularity of the WA-7 with the release of the [[TDL-501 unipod waitress droid]]. The TDL-501 was met with modest success before succumbing to the same changing tastes that doomed the original WA-7.<ref name="TNEGtD" />

==Behind the scenes==
Mondeo Modernism was introduced in ''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]'', a [[2006]] reference book written by [[Daniel Wallace]].<ref name="TNEGtD" /> The author imagined it as a combination of elements from both [[Wikipedia:Art Deco|Art Deco]] and [[Wikipedia:Googie architecture|Googie]].<ref name="Endnotes">{{Blog|danwallace|53|Endnotes for The New Essential Guide to Droids: PART 2 of 3}}</ref>

The design of the WA-7 waitress droid, which was heavily influenced by Mondeo Modernism [[in-universe]],<ref name="CSWE-WA-7 series" /> was based on sketches by visual-effects concept artist [[Warren Fu]],<ref name="TAoSW">''[[The Art of Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones]]''</ref><ref name="Mythmaking">''[[Mythmaking: Behind the Scenes of Attack of the Clones]]''</ref> who wanted the sexy streamlined automaton to evoke the Googie school of architecture.<ref name="SWC:TP" /> The droid was also inspired by the roller-skating waitresses who serve the patrons of [[Wikipedia:Mel's Drive-In|Mel's Drive-In]] in [[George Lucas]]'s [[1973]] film [[Wikipedia:American Graffiti|''American Graffiti'']].<ref name="Mythmaking" /><ref name="TCoGL">''[[The Cinema of George Lucas]]''</ref>
